title: `cookies().has()` breaks in Route Handlers

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: Runtime
labels.description: Related to Node.js or Edge Runtime with Next.js.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.6.0: Wed Jul  5 22:22:52 PDT 2023; root:xnu-8796.141.3~6/RELEASE_ARM64_T8103
    Binaries:
      Node: 18.17.0
      npm: 9.6.7
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: 8.6.12
    Relevant Packages:
      next: 13.4.16
      eslint-config-next: 13.4.10
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
      typescript: 5.1.6
    Next.js Config:
      output: N/A
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

Middleware / Edge (API routes, runtime)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug

-

### To Reproduce

```ts
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export async function GET() {
  const c = cookies()
  c.set('a', 'a')
  const hasCookie = c.has('a')

  return NextResponse.json({ hasCookie }) // expect { hasCookie: true }
}
```

### Describe the Bug

Using `cookies().has()` in `route.ts` throws error:

```console
- error TypeError: (0 , next_headers__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_1__.cookies)(...).has is not a function
    at GET (webpack-internal:///(rsc)/./src/app/api/route.ts:11:78)
    at ...
```

### Expected Behavior

Return boolean by `has` function.

### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

_No response_

_No response_
